audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty read 8.5/10 'Hard' against a 55.62% win rate over 1183 games.
audit.why: A five-and-a-half point positive win rate is not a hard lane; the mirror rates its Olaf rows 4/10 from Gnar's side, which puts this at a mildly favourable 6/10.
audit.corrected: diffRating to 6/10, with breakdown.difficulty and the final rating line brought in line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Gnar/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Gnar/Skill/Gnar while its own whys said level 3, 4-5 and late are Olaf's.
audit.why: The packet chart is Skill/Gnar/Olaf/Olaf/Gnar/Skill/Olaf and matches the existing why-text row for row; the mirror's ratings (Olaf rows 4/10, late 3/10, level 1 5/10) invert to 6/6/7 and 5 on this side.
audit.corrected: Whole chart flipped as one atomic group in both layers; ratings 5/4/6/6/4/5/7.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] said 'Ragnarok cleanses and immunizes mega-Gnar's AOE stun'.
audit.why: Ragnarok does not cleanse; it grants immunity to disables only for as long as he keeps attacking, and it costs 100/90/80s. The stun is Wallop, Mega Gnar's W — the entry never named it.
audit.corrected: Restated as disable immunity while attacking, named Wallop, and the 100s cost written in so it reads as commit-only.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings give Olaf's W lifesteal or omnivamp ('W sustain', 'W-sustain', 'W-omnivamp').
audit.why: Tough It Out is attack speed plus a SHIELD. The life steal and the attack speed are the passive and scale with MISSING health — which is the reason to commit rather than trade in chip against Gnar's poke.
audit.corrected: Healing reassigned to the missing-health passive throughout; W restated as the shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing, but the Hop interaction is deliberately left un-asserted.
audit.why: The kit file tags Undertow with grounding ('shuts off enemy dashes') while Riot's own Undertow text describes only damage, armour reduction and a slow. Per the trust-the-description rule this is treated as a tooltip-parse misfire, matching the mirror's finding, so nothing here claims the axe denies Hop or Crunch.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late were written in the FIRST person ('a Q I throw', 'stay mine', 'my passive').
audit.why: Every other string on the site is second person, addressed to the reader — the voice break is visible on the page.
audit.corrected: All three paragraphs rewritten in second person with the real ability names.

edits.before: Land the axe slow on Gnar, walk the pickup for the reset, reave the true damage, and W-sustain whatever he answers with.
edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields his answer.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Identify how Gnar contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Undertow's slow answers Boomerang Throw's poke, but mini-Gnar hops out of range — level 1 is a genuine coin flip.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Respect Gnar's GNAR! completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Undertow's slow and Tough It Out's shield win the short trades. Respect his Rage bar, not a clock — the transform is what flips a trade you were already winning.

edits.before: Axe-reset slows perma-stick him while W-omnivamp out-heals his boomerang chip in every short trade.
edits.after: The axe reset perma-slows him while your missing-health lifesteal out-heals his boomerang chip.

edits.after: Ragnarok keeps you disable-immune while you keep attacking, so Wallop's stun cannot peel you off the all-in — but it costs 100s.

edits.after: Black Cleaver / Bramble core makes your axe-reset slows and shielded all-ins oppressive while he is still squishy mini form.

edits.after: Land Reckless Swing every 11s and let the missing-health passive heal it

edits.before: Gnar in mini form is the early annoyance — his boomerang pokes and the return catch chips you, and his hops mean a Q I throw at his feet whiffs if he's already moving. Don't chuck Q at max range hoping; walk him into a wall or minion clump, then Q-slow and close so the slow sticks. Once I hit 2-3 with Q plus E, I land a guaranteed true-damage chunk his poke simply can't sustain back, and my passive attack speed ramps the longer the trade runs.
edits.after: Gnar in mini form is the early annoyance — Boomerang Throw pokes and the return catch chips you, and his Hop means an axe thrown at his feet whiffs if he is already moving. Don't throw Undertow at max range hoping; walk him into a wall or a minion clump, then slow him and close so it sticks. Once you hit 2-3 with Undertow plus Reckless Swing you land a true-damage chunk his poke can't sustain back, and your attack speed ramps as your health drops.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay mine — axe-reset slows let me re-throw Q and perma-stick him while W-omnivamp heals through his boomerang chip. The danger spike is when his Rage bar fills: mega-Gnar's AOE stun can lock my all-in and his hop chains a kill if I've blown Ragnarok. So I respect his bar — when he's about to transform, I hold R, eat the stun on cleanse, and only then commit. With Ragnarok up, mega is just a bigger target I run down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours — the axe reset re-throws Undertow off every pickup and perma-sticks him, and your missing-health lifesteal heals through the boomerang chip. The danger is his Rage bar: Wallop's stun locks your all-in and Crunch chains the kill if Ragnarok is down. So read the bar — when he is about to transform, hold R and commit only once you can swing through the stun. With Ragnarok up, Mega is a bigger target you run down.

edits.before: My flat true damage and short-fight kit fade as the game goes long, and Gnar scales into a teamfight monster — one mega AOE stun on my dive flips a fight. But the 1v1 still favors me if I catch him in mini form on a sidelane: Q-slow, E him, W to out-sustain, and Ragnarok to ignore the stun. I have to convert my early-to-mid lead into towers and dives before his mega frontline carry value outweighs my pick threat.
edits.after: Your flat true damage and short-fight kit fade as the game goes long, and Gnar scales into a teamfight monster — one Wallop stun on your dive flips a fight. But the 1v1 still favours you if you catch him in mini form on a side lane: Undertow, Reckless Swing, Tough It Out for the shield, Ragnarok so the stun can't hold you. Convert the early-to-mid lead into towers before his frontline value outweighs your picks.

notes: Three structural problems beyond the ability names. (1) early/mid/late were first-person — the only strings on this page written that way — and are now second person. (2) The level chart ran Gnar-favoured in five rows against a 55.62% win rate and against its own whys; flipped to the packet chart as one atomic group. (3) diffRating 8.5/10 could not be reconciled with that win rate, so it moves to 6/10 along with the two prose strings that quote it — if the user would rather keep the old number, revert those three edits together. Undertow's grounding flag is NOT used anywhere here: Riot's description does not mention grounding, so the Hop-denial interaction is left unclaimed, same call the mirror made.
